approved: Corporations Amendment (Simple Corporate Bonds and Other Measures) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would make it easier to trade retail corporate bonds in Australia.
It changes the Corporations Act 2001 to reduce compliance costs for issuers of certain retail bonds.
The main changes start on a day set by Proclamation or six months after Royal Assent, while the rest of the bill starts the day after Royal Assent.
The bill amends the Corporations Act 2001.
It facilitates improved trading of retail corporate bonds.
It reduces compliance costs for issuers of certain retail corporate bonds.
Issuers of certain retail corporate bonds.

Supported the Corporations Amendment (Simple Corporate Bonds and Other Measures) Bill 2014, which simplifies retail bond prospectuses and extends the maximum bond term from 10 to 15 years, noting a 2012 Reserve Bank estimate that Australia's corporate bond market was worth around $825 billion, of which retail investors held less than one per cent.

Declared that the Corporations Amendment (Simple Corporate Bonds and Other Measures) Bill 2014 and the Meteorology Amendment (Online Advertising) Bill 2014 were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Supported the corporate bonds bill as effectively Labor's own legislation, citing BHP Billiton's $1 billion five-year bond raised in 2012 and Qantas's $175 million seven-year bond raised in May 2013 as recent examples of local corporate debt issuance the reform aims to encourage.
